extraction.name: LUMA: A Benchmark Dataset for Learning from Uncertain and Multimodal Data
extraction.description: A multimodal dataset featuring audio, image, and textual data from 50 classes, specifically designed for learning from uncertain data. It extends the CIFAR 10/100 dataset with audio samples extracted from three audio corpora, and text data generated using the Gemma-7B Large Language Model. The dataset enables controlled injection of varying types and degrees of uncertainty for experiments and benchmarking initiatives.
extraction.creator: Grigor Bezirganyan, Sana Sellami, Laure Berti-Équille, Sébastien Fournier
extraction.citeAs: Grigor Bezirganyan, Sana Sellami, Laure Berti-Équille, and Sébastien Fournier. 2025. LUMA: A Benchmark Dataset for Learning from Uncertain and Multimodal Data. In Proceedings of the 48th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval (SIGIR '25), July 13–18, 2025, Padua, Italy. ACM, New York, NY, USA, 10 pages. https://doi.org/10.1145/3726302.3730302
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset includes 101,000 images from CIFAR 10/100, 135,096 speech audio recordings extracted from three audio corpora (The Spoken Wikipedia, LibriSpeech, and Mozilla Common Voice), and 62,875 text passages generated using the Gemma-7B Instruct Large Language Model. Each modality is independently sourced, reflecting real-world conditions where data is often collected under different conditions and times.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator, Web API
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images were compiled from the CIFAR 10/100 dataset. Audio samples were extracted from The Spoken Wikipedia (hundreds of hours of phoneme-level aligned audio from volunteer readers reading Wikipedia articles), LibriSpeech (1,000 hours of English speech derived from audiobooks from the LibriVox project), and Mozilla Common Voice (crowdsourced open-source collection of voices by volunteer contributors from around the world). Text data was generated using the Gemma-7B Instruct Large Language Model based on class labels.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For audio modality, word-level alignments were used to extract audio segments corresponding to CIFAR-10/100 class labels. For LibriSpeech and Mozilla Common Voice, force-aligned alignments were generated using Montreal Forced Aligner. Class label set was extended with plural forms of words. For text modality, all label occurrences were masked and fed back into the Gemma-7B Instruct model for validation. For classes with gender bias (man, woman, boy, girl), prompts were reconstructed to explicitly provide topics and keywords with occupations to minimize bias.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images: 42 classes were chosen with at least 600 samples per class after alignment with other modalities, and 8 classes with less than 600 samples were designated as OOD samples. Audio: Extracted audio segments were validated using OpenAI's Whisper Large V3 model for automatic transcription validation. Samples where transcription matched the class label were considered valid. Text: Generated texts were validated by masking label occurrences and using Gemma-7B Instruct to classify the text. Samples where prediction matched ground truth were accepted. Deep features were extracted from each modality (Wav2Vec for audio, BERT for text, VGG-11 for images) for diversity control.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For audio validation, manual annotation was performed for samples that failed automatic validation. The labeling interface provided the audio sample with the prompt 'Is the audio saying the word below? (An extra 's' or 'es' in the pronunciation is okay.)' with answer options of 'Yes' or 'No'. Two annotations per sample were collected from 17 annotators. Samples were accepted where both annotators confirmed validity (71.61% annotation agreement). Samples with conflicting annotations were rejected.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For audio validation, 2 annotations per sample were collected. 71.61% annotation agreement was achieved. Samples were accepted only when both annotators confirmed the validity of the sample. Samples with conflicting annotations were rejected.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 2 annotations per audio sample for manual validation
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: M.Sc. and PhD students, and professors with advanced to fluent English knowledge
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: OpenAI's Whisper Large V3 model for audio transcription validation, Gemma-7B Instruct for text validation and bias detection, Montreal Forced Aligner for generating word-level alignments
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Gender bias was identified in text data, particularly for classes 'man', 'woman', 'boy', and 'girl'. The Gemma model identified high levels of gender bias in these classes. The authors noted that describing a man or woman in an unbiased way is a challenging task for LLM models trained on unbalanced data. Prompts were reconstructed to minimize bias by explicitly providing topics and keywords with occupations. After reconstruction, significant bias still existed but enough unbiased texts were identified for inclusion in the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Since textual data was generated using an LLM, the dataset may contain factual inaccuracies or biases. The dataset shall not be used as a source of knowledge or information. For audio data, since most samples are collected from forced alignments, it is possible to have misaligned audio segments which could introduce additional noise. Some audio samples may be very noisy or have strong accents which can be hard to interpret.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is specifically designed for benchmarking multimodal learning algorithms on uncertain data and for developing, evaluating, and benchmarking trustworthy and robust multimodal deep learning approaches. Use cases include Training, Testing, and Validation. Each generated version consists of 600 data records per class (500 for training, and 100 for testing) belonging to 42 classes, and 3,859 OOD data points belonging to the remaining 8 classes. The dataset is intended to promote and support the development of trustworthy and robust machine learning approaches for safety critical applications.
